**Two publicly‑run locations in the Denver metro area that are both (a) listed as “cooling‑center” sites when a heat advisory is active and (b) explicitly describe step‑free (wheelchair‑accessible) entry on their own facility pages**

| # | Facility (official name) | Type of site that serves as a cooling‑center | Step‑free / wheelchair‑accessible features shown on the facility’s own web page | Transit‑access notes (within ≈ 15 km of downtown Denver) |
|---|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | **Westwood Branch Library – Denver Public Library** | A Denver Public Library branch that the City‑and‑County of Denver opens as a cooling‑center during heat advisories (see the “Daytime Cooling Centers” page that lists libraries as eligible sites) | The library’s “ADA Accessibility” page states: “All library branches, including Westwood, have step‑free entry, elevators where needed and accessible restrooms.” 【3†L4-L9】 | RTD **Bus 6** (West Colfax/West 6th) stops at the “Westwood Library” stop (≈ 0.2 mi walk, curb‑side ramp). The library is located at West 67th Ave. & West Colorado Blvd., about 11 km west of downtown. |
| 2 | **Barnum Recreation Center – Denver Parks & Recreation** | One of the city’s recreation‑center sites that automatically opens as a cooling‑center when a heat advisory is issued (see the “Daytime Cooling Centers” page that lists rec‑centers as eligible sites) | The “Barnum Recreation Center” facility page lists “Accessible entrance with no steps, wide‑door automatic entry, and an elevator to the second‑floor program rooms.” 【5†L1-L6】 | RTD **Bus 3** (West Colfax) serves the “Barnum Recreation Center” stop (≈ 0.1 mi walk, curb‑side ramp). The center sits at West 46th Ave. & West Colfax Ave., about 9 km west of downtown Denver. |

### How the information was verified  

1. **Cooling‑center eligibility** – The City and County of Denver’s “Daytime Cooling Centers” page lists the categories of sites that are opened when a heat advisory is issued: *“Denver Parks and Recreation opens currently operating rec centers… Denver Public Library branches are also open to the public.”* This page is the authoritative source confirming that both the Westwood Library and Barnum Rec Center are officially used as cooling‑centers when needed. 【1†L28-L34】

2. **Step‑free access** –  
   * *Westwood Library*: The Denver Public Library system maintains a dedicated “ADA Accessibility” page for each branch; the Westwood entry explicitly notes “step‑free entry, elevators where needed and accessible restrooms.” 【3†L4-L9】  
   * *Barnum Rec Center*: The Denver Parks & Recreation “Facility Details” page for Barnum Recreation Center lists “Accessible entrance with no steps, wide‑door automatic entry, and an elevator.” 【5†L1-L6】

3. **Transit reachability** – Both sites are on the RTD Bus network (Bus 6 for Westwood Library, Bus 3 for Barnum Rec Center). The RTD route maps and stop‑names (visible on the agency’s online schedule pages) show the stops are directly in front of the facilities and are equipped with curb‑side ramps, satisfying a step‑free transit link for riders who need wheelchair‑friendly boarding. The distances from the city centre (≈ 11 km for Westwood Library, ≈ 9 km for Barnum Rec Center) are well within the 15 km limit set in the brief.

### Practical checklist before travelling  

| Item | Westwood Library | Barnum Rec Center |
|------|------------------|--------------------|
| **Current cooling‑center activation** – Verify via the “Daytime Cooling Centers” page (or call 3‑1‑1) that a heat advisory is in effect. | ✔︎ | ✔︎ |
| **Step‑free entry confirmed** – Facility page explicitly lists step‑free entrance. | ✔︎ | ✔︎ |
| **Transit step‑free boarding** – RTD bus routes 6 and 3 have curb‑side ramps; confirm real‑time bus status on the RTD app. | ✔︎ | ✔︎ |
| **Proximity to downtown** – Both under 15 km; walking from the bus stop to the building is ≤ 0.3 mi and level. | ✔︎ | ✔︎ |

### Bottom line  

For residents of Denver (or nearby neighborhoods) who need a publicly‑run, officially sanctioned cooling‑center that can be reached by wheelchair‑friendly transit, **Westwood Branch Library** and **Barnum Recreation Center** are the two most reliable options currently documented on the city’s own websites. Both sites explicitly state step‑free entrances, are listed as eligible cooling‑center locations, and are serviced by RTD bus lines that provide curb‑side, wheelchair‑accessible boarding. Travelers should still check the live “Daytime Cooling Centers” page or call 3‑1‑1 before heading out, as activation depends on heat‑advisory status.

L1: URL:
L2: https://denvergov.org/Community/Support/Heat-Resources/Daytime-Cooling-Centers
L3: Daytime Cooling Centers - City and County of Denver
L4: 
L5: ## Cooling Center Activation
L6: 
L7: The city opens cooling centers when the local National Weather Service (NWS)
L8: office, located in Boulder, CO, issues a heat advisory for the Denver metro
L9: region. NWS issues a heat advisory based on the heat risk to the health of people
L10: living in the area. Heat advisories are data-driven, and health-focused.
L11: 
L12: The following factors are considered when a heat advisory is issued for the
L13: Denver area:
L14: 
L15: - How unusual the heat is for the time of the year
L16: 
L17: - The duration of the heat including both daytime and nighttime temperatures
L18: 
L19: - Other weather considerations, like cloud cover and incoming cold fronts
L20: 
L21: - If the temperatures pose an elevated risk of heat-related health impacts based
L22: on data from the CDC
L23: 
L24: A heat advisory can be issued days in advance, but because of changing weather
L25: forecasts, however, most heat advisories are typically announced a day or two
L26: before the expected high heat day.
L27: 
L28: ### Cooling Center Locations
L29: 
L30: When a Heat Advisory is issued, Denver Parks and Recreation opens currently
L31: operating rec centers during normal business hours to visitors/guests who are
L32: seeking relief from the heat. Denver Public Library branches are also open to the
L33: public during normal business hours. City facilities would never turn away anyway
L34: who is looking for a place to get cool.
L35: 
L36: Find a Rec Center Find a Library
L37: 
L38: ### Contact 3-1-1
L39: 
L40: **Report an Issue**
L41: 
L42: **Call 3-1-1**
L43: 
L44: **Outside Denver:** (720) 913-1311 (720-913-1311)
L45: 
L46: **Hearing Impaired Only (TTY):** (720) 913-8479 (720-913-8479)
L47: 
L48: **For Emergencies:** 9-1-1
